stem: Why does light gray body text on a white background present an accessibility barrier for people with low vision?

options.text: It lacks sufficient contrast for people with reduced contrast sensitivity to differentiate letters from the page.
options.rationale: People with low vision frequently experience reduced contrast sensitivity, making faint text blend into backgrounds.

options.text: It reduces the effective font size, so readers with low vision need to enlarge the page to read it.
options.rationale: Low contrast does not change font size; it reduces the difference in luminance between text and background.

options.text: It makes the text harder for screen readers to interpret because they rely on color to separate letters from the page.
options.rationale: Screen readers read the underlying text regardless of color; the barrier is visual contrast, not the text's availability to assistive technology.

options.text: It prevents users from applying their own high-contrast browser or operating-system settings to the page.
options.rationale: Browser and operating-system contrast settings can override authored colors; the problem is the default contrast the author chose.

explanation: Low vision often involves reduced contrast sensitivity, so light gray text against a white background provides too little luminance difference for many readers to perceive the words.

references.title: Web Accessibility Initiative: Diverse Abilities and Barriers — Visual
